checks.claim: Signed in 2022, SB 177 defines a microreactor (up to 50 MWe) and exempts it from the legislative land-designation step before siting permits; the implementing regulations arrived in August 2025, giving organized boroughs direct approval authority with standard setbacks retained. The date split matters for citation accuracy: statute 2022, regulations 2025.
checks.evidence: World Nuclear News (28 Jul 2023) says Alaska's 2022 updates to AS 18.45 define a microreactor as an advanced nuclear reactor capable of producing no more than 50 MW, that Gov. Dunleavy signed SB 177 in 2022, and that the implementing regulations come into effect in August 2023. akbizmag (2 Aug 2023) says streamlined regulations are now in place and that SB 177 removed the legislative approval requirement, except in the Unorganized Borough. No fetched page supports an August 2025 regulation date.
checks.correction: Signed in 2022, SB 177 defines a microreactor (up to 50 MW) and removes the legislative siting approval step outside the Unorganized Borough; the implementing regulations took effect in August 2023.

dockets.what_it_says: The Micro-Reactor Incentive Act directs the NJ Board of Public Utilities to develop a competitive solicitation program for awarding micro-reactor incentive contracts. The bill text defines a micro-reactor as a nuclear fission reactor with a rated electric generating capacity of not more than 20 megawatts. It was introduced 2026-10-19 and referred to the Senate Environment and Energy Committee; the fetched text gives no cost, cost-recovery mechanism or capacity target.
dockets.microreactor_read: A state solicitation for reactors up to 20 MW would be a new buyer path in New Jersey, but the bill has only been referred to committee.

items.headline: NRC finalizes rule letting reactor applicants use DOE and DoW authorization data
items.what_happened: The NRC finalized a rule titled 'NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by U.S. Department of Energy or Department of War' on 2026-10-22. It adds Section 50.43(f) to 10 CFR Part 50 and revises Section 53.440(a)(1) in Part 53 so that an application may use information gathered from a DOE- or DOW-authorized reactor. The NRC says the rule does not let it forgo an independent review.
items.why_it_matters: A vendor with a DOE-authorized test unit can point to that operating record in an NRC application, which may shorten review. Reliance depends on how closely the tested unit matches the commercial design.
items.binding_note: Final rule. Power Magazine reports the NRC expected Federal Register publication in the week of Oct. 26, with effect 30 days after publication; publication was not verified. Orrick's article does not state an effective date.
